groups.reason: The recalled scepter destruction is recorded at Vetta in the Skaer Islands, but that does not establish which place name was uttered here or rule out a spoken misremembering. The complete marked replacement remains unclear.
The DM supplies the forgotten name of the ancient elven opponent of Apollyon, immediately repeated by Delwath. Arheste uniquely matches that visit and role, despite the poor phonetic rendering.
Delwath repeats the supplied name of the ancient elf interviewed about Apollyon; Arheste and the recorded Orenlas visit match the full description.
The protective divine light follows Riswynn's feast and refers to the dwarven gods, whose documented name is Bahrâzel.
The listed forge metals match the recovered forge inventory, which explicitly names fey steel.

The recalled deception resembles the recorded trick at Uzgukhar, but the marker could reflect ordinary wording such as orc city or a different reference. Evidence does not establish a complete proper-name replacement.
Ordinary chatter, numbers, rules explanations, or damaged spellcasting wording without a clear standalone name or setting term; reconstructing these spans is outside names-v1.

The exchange interrupts a statement about killing a dragon as Kong joins. This may contain a greeting to Kong, but the marked span and adjacent words do not establish a complete standalone name replacement.
The hoard inventory gives this exact silver vial inscription and establishes the name Serandris.
The dagger with sight-related magic is identified as Urskan by its reference note, establishing Ursk as the place named here.
The immediate exchange names Vindristjarna while discussing the danger posed by automated defensive towers to the ship. The shortened recognition is strongly favored as that same named skyship.
Willow is expressing fear for a companion and herself, then the rest of the party. Wellby is the strongly favored personal referent; the ordinary noun well-being is less natural in this construction.
